body:
Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Derive current versus time and interpret the inductor voltage immediately after switching.

(b) Determine total heat dissipated and explain the inductor's role in current continuity.

Stimulus:
An inductor L carries steady current I₀. The source is removed and the inductor discharges through resistor R. Take v_L(t) to be measured with the same polarity reference that was used while the source was driving current through the inductor during steady state (positive at the terminal where current entered).

Question stem:
A conducting plate entering a magnetic-field region experiences a force opposing motion because

Choices:
A. eddy currents obey Lenz's law
B. eddy currents reinforce the increasing magnetic flux
C. magnetic fields do positive work directly
D. electrical resistance directly exerts a backward mechanical force

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Design a feasible measurement that tests the LR circuit's current-growth relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

(b) State the governing principle (Kirchhoff's voltage law) and explain what role the initial condition I(0)=0 plays in this measurement of the time constant L/R -- and whether it is necessary for a valid measurement of τ.

Stimulus:
An LR circuit with inductance L and resistance R is connected to constant emf ℰ at t=0 with I(0)=0.

Question stem:
An ideal LC circuit has angular frequency ω equal to:

Choices:
A. LC
B. 1/LC
C. \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}\)
D. \(\sqrt{LC}\)

Question stem:
Induced electric fields from changing magnetic flux are

Choices:
A. conservative with zero circulation
B. nonconservative with nonzero circulation
C. always radial
D. always zero in vacuum

Question stem:
Energy stored in an ideal inductor carrying current I is

Choices:
A. \(LI^{2}\)
B. \((1/2)LI^{2}\)
C. \(2LI^{2}\)
D. \((1/4)LI^{2}\)

Question stem:
Magnetic braking of a sliding rod: Answer all mandatory subparts. Show reasoning and calculations clearly. Use standard AP Physics notation and justify qualitative claims.

Parts:
Predict the induced-current direction as viewed from above and the magnetic-force direction on the rod. Justify from flux change and energy.
Derive the differential equation for v(t) and solve for the rod's speed.
Sketch speed and resistor power versus time on labeled axes, and determine the total energy dissipated in the resistor.

Stimulus:
A conducting rod of length ℓ and mass m slides without mechanical friction on horizontal conducting rails. The rails are connected by a resistor R, forming a closed loop. A uniform magnetic field B points vertically downward. At t=0 the rod is moving right with speed v0. Neglect rail and rod resistance and self-inductance.

Question stem:
For an LR circuit connected to a DC source, current approaches steady state with time constant

Choices:
A. L/R
B. R/L
C. LR
D. 1/LR

Question stem:
Answer all parts of the following question.

(a) Translate the LR circuit's governing differential equation into a labeled graph of current versus time, and explain what its initial slope and final asymptotic value represent.

(b) Explain how Kirchhoff's voltage law (the governing principle) and the initial condition I(0)=0 with constant emf ℰ (the stated assumption) yield the current's approach to ℰ/R.

Stimulus:
An LR circuit with inductance L and resistance R is connected to constant emf ℰ at t=0 with I(0)=0.

Question stem:
Uniform B crosses a single loop of area A at angle θ to the area normal. Flux is

Choices:
A. BA sinθ
B. BA cosθ
C. BA
D. 2BA cosθ
